policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders the place name "Zaanannim", transliterating the qere בְּצַעֲנַנִּים with its full nun-nun sequence (Zaanan-nim). The ketiv בצענים lacks that second nun and would yield "Zaanaim"; the ASV spelling excludes it. The verse's other notes are a hebrew_gloss on Kain and two alternative_rendering notes (father-in-law, terebinth), none of which bear on this lemma.
